title: Jesus didn’t need mud.
paragraphs: Jesus didn’t need mud.
Let that sit with you for a moment.

The One who spoke light into existence…
The One who formed man from dust in the beginning…
The One who opened blind eyes with a word in other moments…
—chose dirt and spit.

Not because He lacked power.
But because He was revealing something deeper than power.

In John 9, we meet a man who had never seen light.
Not blurred vision. Not partial sight.
Complete darkness… from birth.
And the disciples ask the question many of us still ask today:
“Who sinned?”

They were looking for blame.
Jesus was about to reveal purpose.

“Neither this man nor his parents sinned,” He said,
“but this happened so that the works of God might be displayed in him.” (John 9:3)
Then something unexpected happens.

Jesus kneels.
Touches the ground.
Spits into the dust.
Forms mud with His hands…
…and places it on the man’s eyes.
Pause there.
Because this is where most people miss it.
Why mud?
Why not just speak?
Why not instantly restore what was missing?

Because sometimes God doesn’t just want to heal you…
He wants to involve you.
The method is part of the message.

In Genesis, God formed man from the dust of the ground.
Now in John 9, Jesus uses dust again—but this time not to create life…
To restore what was broken.

This wasn’t random.
This was intentional.

It was as if Jesus was saying:
“The same God who formed you… can reform you.”
But then comes the part that challenges us:
“Go. Wash in the Pool of Siloam.”
The miracle wasn’t finished yet.
Imagine this moment.

The man still can’t see.
Now his eyes are covered in mud.
People are watching. Whispering. Judging.
And Jesus tells him to walk.

No proof yet.
No visible change.
No guarantee—except the word of Jesus.
This is where faith becomes real.

Because it’s easy to celebrate miracles…
but harder to obey instructions that don’t make sense.
He had to move while still blind.
He had to trust before he saw.

He had to walk through public uncertainty
with private hope.
And somewhere between the command and the water…
his miracle was waiting.
Read that again.

Not in the mud.
Not even in the moment of touch.
But in the place of obedience.
“So he went and washed, and came home seeing.” (John 9:7)

He didn’t argue.
He didn’t delay.
He didn’t demand understanding.
He moved.
And that movement unlocked what the miracle started.
Here’s the truth many of us need to hear:
Delayed clarity is not denied purpose.

God will sometimes ask you to take steps
that feel uncomfortable…
illogical…
even embarrassing…
—not to confuse you, but to transform you.
Because obedience does something miracles alone cannot.
It builds trust.
It shifts your dependence.
It aligns your heart with His voice.
And sometimes…

the greatest breakthrough in your life
is waiting on the other side of a simple instruction.

Naaman almost missed his healing because the method felt too simple.
The Israelites missed moments because obedience felt too costly.
And even today, many delay their breakthrough…

not because God is silent,
but because His instructions don’t match their expectations.
But this man?
He walked anyway.

Blind… but moving.
Uncertain… but obeying.
Covered in mud… but full of faith.
And when he washed…
everything changed.
Not just his sight.
His identity.
His testimony.
His encounter with Jesus became undeniable.
And here’s what makes this even more powerful:
Later in the chapter, when questioned, the man didn’t have all the theology figured out…
But he had an experience no one could argue with:
“I was blind… but now I see.” (John 9:25)
That’s what obedience produces.

Not just results—
but testimony.
So here’s the question:

What if the “mud” in your life…
is not a delay…
but a setup?

What if the uncomfortable instruction…
is actually the pathway to your clarity?

What if God is not just trying to fix something in you…
but reveal something through you?
Because sometimes…

God will use what feels unnecessary
to accomplish what is eternal.
Clarity often comes after movement—not before it.

And the miracle you’re waiting for
may be waiting on your obedience.

So if He says “go”…
even when you don’t fully understand…
Go.

Because on the other side of that step
might be the moment you finally see.

Engagement Question:
What is something God has been prompting you to do lately—even if it doesn’t fully make sense yet?
